correctness.rationale: Represent the centered simplex vertices by coordinate differences. Two faces I,J have trivial direction-space intersection exactly if |I∩J|≤1 (by affine independence); disjoint face spaces are orthogonal. For |I∩J|=1 their basis Gram blocks, after common scaling, equal I_r+J_r, I_s+J_s and cross block all ones. Since (I_r+J_r)^−1=I_r−J_r/(r+1), the largest cosine is √[r/(r+1)]√[s/(s+1)]. The permissible r+s≤n maximizes at r+s=n; balancing the positive integers uniquely maximizes rs/((r+1)(s+1)), proving all n≥2 and equality cases. Algebra gives 1−c²=(n+1)/((r+1)(s+1)), and insertion into the source M formula yields the stated radius. Inspected all actual proof and verifier code, including finite exact rank n≤6 and dimension comparisons n≤100, auxiliary only.

final_claim: For a regular Euclidean n-simplex (n≥2), its maximum principal cosine over nonintersecting positive-dimensional face-direction spaces is √[rs/((r+1)(s+1))] with r=⌊n/2⌋, s=⌈n/2⌉, uniquely at balanced shared-vertex face pairs exhausting n+1 vertices. The inherited sufficient exceptional radius is (1+√[(r+1)(s+1)/(n+1)])/2, without a minimal-radius assertion.
limitations: Only Euclidean regular simplices and source-inherited sufficient cutoff.
